title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
statement_short: Design a data structure that supports adding new words and searching if a string matches any previously added string. Search queries may contain '.' dots, where '.' can match any single letter.
constraints: 1 <= word.length <= 25, word in addWord consists of lowercase English letters, word in search consists of '.' or lowercase letters, at most 10^4 calls
hint: Word length up to 25 with wildcard '.' matching favors a character trie combined with recursive DFS branch exploration.
why_not: Right: Trie combined with recursive child branching for '.' dot characters evaluates wildcard prefix queries in O(L) best-case time. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing words in a hash set handles exact lookups in O(L), but wildcard '.' searches require checking every stored word in O(N \* L) time. Not Backtracking: Exhaustive string pattern matching without a prefix tree requires scanning the full dictionary. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointers cannot match character wildcards across multi-branch dictionaries natively.
complexity: O(L) time for add, O(26^L) worst for wildcard search, O(N \* L) space
